hypothesis: The public trainer can replay our reconstructed fixture trace with the shipped BF16 weights and reproduce every live corrected integer probability, without training.
method: Build public replay trainer with original precise floating-point policy and the live compiler/SIMD support. Separately compile the compressor deterministic-math source with its recorded DETNUM_CXXFLAGS and link it into replay. Model code and input traces stay unchanged. Load shipped BF16 model, REPLAY_FREEZE_AT=1; no full backward window or optimizer step occurs. Compare every integer output and a wrong-first-probability control.
acceptance: Accepted unchanged-archive trace comparison with exact original XML restoration and encoder/decoder trace identity
Complete source, compiler, binary, weights, trace and log provenance
Every corrected integer probability equals the live reference, exact full trace count and no extra probability/channel records
Deliberately wrong first probability is rejected at bit zero as a value mismatch
Both fixed fixtures must pass before proposing a training experiment; preserve any failure
limitations: Frozen fixture inference only. Does not check post-thaw online gradient updates or optimizer equivalence.
No original historical trace is available for comparison.
A passing Mac comparison does not establish Linux numerical parity.
Replay loss is not an archive size; no changed weights, improvement or prize score is established.
storage: Raw traces and replay binaries stay local; commit small provenance reports and logs.
